lessons.title: Making plans
lessons.summary: Suggest an activity, agree on a time, and change a plan politely.
lessons.heroTitle: Turn an idea into a real plan.
lessons.completionTitle: You can arrange a meeting in German.
objectives: Suggest an activity with wollen or können
Agree on a day and time
Cancel or rearrange a plan politely

sentences.text: Wollen wir uns am Samstag treffen?
sentences.translation: Shall we meet on Saturday?
sentences.note: Wollen wir is a direct but friendly way to suggest a shared plan.

sentences.text: Ich schlage das neue Café vor.
sentences.translation: I suggest the new café.
sentences.note: The prefix vor moves to the end in a main clause.

sentences.text: Passt dir vier Uhr?
sentences.translation: Does four o'clock work for you?
sentences.note: Dir identifies the person for whom the time is suitable.

sentences.text: Leider muss ich absagen.
sentences.translation: Unfortunately, I have to cancel.
sentences.note: Leider softens disappointing information.

sentences.text: Vielleicht klappt es am Sonntag.
sentences.translation: Maybe Sunday will work.
sentences.note: Klappt es is a common conversational way to say that something works out.

grammar.title: Separable verbs in plans
grammar.explanation: In a main clause, the prefix of a separable verb goes to the end. With a modal verb, the full infinitive stays together at the end.
grammar.pattern: Ich schlage etwas vor. / Ich muss leider absagen.

examples.source: Mira schlägt einen Spaziergang vor.
examples.translation: Mira suggests a walk.

examples.source: Wir müssen das Treffen absagen.
examples.translation: We have to cancel the meeting.

grammar.commonMistake: Do not separate the verb after a modal: say wir müssen absagen, not wir müssen sagen ab.

Vorschlagen separates into schlage ... vor.

Vielleicht means maybe or perhaps.

Das passt confirms that the proposed time works.

lessons.title: A weekend away
lessons.summary: Describe a short trip and talk about what happened in the past.
lessons.heroTitle: Bring a past weekend to life.
lessons.completionTitle: You can describe a short trip.
objectives: Name common parts of a short journey
Build the perfect tense with haben and sein
Tell events in a clear sequence

sentences.text: Wir sind nach Hamburg gefahren.
sentences.translation: We traveled to Hamburg.
sentences.note: Movement verbs such as fahren usually form the perfect tense with sein.

sentences.text: Ich habe ein kleines Hotel gebucht.
sentences.translation: I booked a small hotel.
sentences.note: Most transitive verbs form the perfect tense with haben.

sentences.text: Dort haben wir Freunde besucht.
sentences.translation: We visited friends there.
sentences.note: The time or place can come first, followed by the conjugated verb.

sentences.text: Am Abend sind wir lange spazieren gegangen.
sentences.translation: In the evening, we went for a long walk.
sentences.note: Gehen uses sein in the perfect tense.

sentences.text: Die Reise hat uns sehr gut gefallen.
sentences.translation: We liked the trip very much.
sentences.note: Gefallen uses the dative pronoun uns for the people who liked it.

grammar.title: The perfect tense with haben and sein
grammar.explanation: Use haben with most verbs. Use sein mainly with movement or a change of state. The past participle normally appears at the end of the clause.

examples.source: Ich habe ein Zimmer gebucht.
examples.translation: I booked a room.

examples.source: Wir sind nach Hamburg gefahren.
examples.translation: We traveled to Hamburg.

grammar.commonMistake: Do not use haben with fahren when it describes travel: say wir sind gefahren.

lessons.title: Finding a flat
lessons.summary: Compare homes, explain your priorities, and arrange a viewing.
lessons.heroTitle: Find a place that feels right.
lessons.completionTitle: You can discuss a flat and your priorities.
objectives: Understand common housing vocabulary
Compare two homes with comparative forms
Give a reason with weil

sentences.text: Die Wohnung ist heller als die andere.
sentences.translation: The flat is brighter than the other one.
sentences.note: Use the comparative adjective plus als to compare unequal things.

sentences.text: Mir ist eine ruhige Lage wichtig.
sentences.translation: A quiet location is important to me.
sentences.note: Mir ist ... wichtig expresses a personal priority.

sentences.text: Ich möchte umziehen, weil die Miete zu hoch ist.
sentences.translation: I want to move because the rent is too high.
sentences.note: In a weil clause, the conjugated verb moves to the end.

sentences.text: Ist die Wohnung noch frei?
sentences.translation: Is the flat still available?
sentences.note: Frei is commonly used for an available room or flat.

sentences.text: Wann ist eine Besichtigung möglich?
sentences.translation: When is a viewing possible?
sentences.note: This is a polite, concise question for a landlord or agent.

grammar.title: Giving reasons with weil
grammar.explanation: Weil introduces a reason. In the weil clause, the conjugated verb moves to the end. A comma separates the main clause and the reason.

examples.source: Ich ziehe um, weil die Wohnung zu klein ist.
examples.translation: I am moving because the flat is too small.

examples.source: Die Lage gefällt mir, weil sie ruhig ist.
examples.translation: I like the location because it is quiet.

grammar.commonMistake: After weil, put the conjugated verb at the end: weil die Miete hoch ist.

lessons.title: Smart shopping
lessons.summary: Ask for another size, try something on, and handle a return politely.
lessons.heroTitle: Find what fits and ask with confidence.
lessons.completionTitle: You can manage a clothing purchase in German.
objectives: Ask for a different size or color
Describe how an item fits
Request an exchange with a receipt

sentences.text: Kann ich die Jacke anprobieren?
sentences.translation: Can I try on the jacket?
sentences.note: The full infinitive anprobieren stays together after kann.

sentences.text: Haben Sie sie auch in einer größeren Größe?
sentences.translation: Do you also have it in a larger size?
sentences.note: Sie replaces the feminine noun die Jacke.

sentences.text: Der Pullover passt mir leider nicht.
sentences.translation: Unfortunately, the sweater does not fit me.
sentences.note: Passen takes the dative pronoun mir for the person.

sentences.text: Ist dieser Mantel reduziert?
sentences.translation: Is this coat reduced?
sentences.note: Dieser matches the masculine noun Mantel.

sentences.text: Ich möchte das Hemd mit der Quittung umtauschen.
sentences.translation: I would like to exchange the shirt with the receipt.
sentences.note: Möchte makes the request polite and the infinitive remains at the end.

grammar.title: Asking for a different size
grammar.explanation: Use the comparative adjective with an ending when you need a different version of an item. After in with a location, einer größeren Größe uses the dative case.

examples.source: Haben Sie das in einer kleineren Größe?
examples.translation: Do you have that in a smaller size?

examples.source: Ich brauche einen größeren Pullover.
examples.translation: I need a larger sweater.

grammar.commonMistake: Do not leave the comparative adjective without its case ending: say in einer größeren Größe.

lessons.title: Finding the way
lessons.summary: Understand directions, change transport, and confirm where a place is.
lessons.heroTitle: Move through the city without getting lost.
lessons.completionTitle: You can ask for and follow directions.
objectives: Ask where a destination is
Follow a sequence of directions
Explain where to change transport

sentences.text: Gehen Sie bis zur nächsten Kreuzung geradeaus.
sentences.translation: Go straight ahead to the next intersection.
sentences.note: The formal imperative uses the verb followed by Sie.

sentences.text: Biegen Sie dann links ab.
sentences.translation: Then turn left.
sentences.note: In the imperative, the separable prefix ab appears at the end.

sentences.text: Die Apotheke liegt gegenüber dem Bahnhof.
sentences.translation: The pharmacy is opposite the train station.
sentences.note: Gegenüber takes the dative form dem Bahnhof.

sentences.text: Wo muss ich in die U-Bahn umsteigen?
sentences.translation: Where do I have to change to the underground?
sentences.note: After muss, the full infinitive umsteigen goes to the end.

sentences.text: Steigen Sie an der dritten Haltestelle aus.
sentences.translation: Get off at the third stop.
sentences.note: An der describes a location and uses the dative case.

grammar.title: Giving formal directions
grammar.explanation: Build the formal imperative with the verb first and Sie immediately after it. Separable prefixes still move to the end of the instruction.

examples.source: Gehen Sie geradeaus.
examples.translation: Go straight ahead.

examples.source: Steigen Sie am Marktplatz aus.
examples.translation: Get off at the market square.

grammar.commonMistake: Keep Sie after the verb and capitalize it; do not use the statement order Sie gehen.

reading.title: The quickest route

lines.speaker: Besucher
lines.text: Entschuldigung, wie komme ich zum Stadtmuseum?
lines.translation: Excuse me, how do I get to the city museum?

lines.speaker: Passantin
lines.text: Gehen Sie bis zur Kreuzung geradeaus und biegen Sie rechts ab.
lines.translation: Go straight to the intersection and turn right.

lines.speaker: Besucher
lines.text: Ist es weit von hier?
lines.translation: Is it far from here?

lines.speaker: Passantin
lines.text: Nein. Das Museum liegt gegenüber der nächsten Bushaltestelle.
lines.translation: No. The museum is opposite the next bus stop.

questions.explanation: Umsteigen means to change from one train, bus, or line to another.
The formal imperative begins with the verb, followed by Sie.
Gegenüber takes the dative; Bahnhof is masculine, so dem is correct.
Die Kreuzung means intersection.
The formal imperative uses Gehen Sie.
Aussteigen separates into steigen ... aus.

questions.prompt: Ask how to reach the museum.
questions.explanation: Wie komme ich zu ...? is the standard way to ask for a route.

lessons.title: Everyday health help
lessons.summary: Describe common symptoms, arrange an appointment, and understand simple advice.
lessons.heroTitle: Explain how you feel and get the right help.
lessons.completionTitle: You can handle a simple health conversation.
objectives: Describe how long a symptom has lasted
Arrange a medical appointment
Understand advice with sollen

sentences.text: Ich habe seit gestern Halsschmerzen.
sentences.translation: I have had a sore throat since yesterday.
sentences.note: German normally uses the present tense with seit for an ongoing condition.

sentences.text: Haben Sie heute noch einen Termin frei?
sentences.translation: Do you still have an appointment available today?
sentences.note: Einen Termin frei haben means to have an available appointment.

sentences.text: Ich fühle mich müde und habe leichtes Fieber.
sentences.translation: I feel tired and have a slight fever.
sentences.note: Sich fühlen is reflexive and uses mich with ich.

sentences.text: Sie sollten viel trinken und sich ausruhen.
sentences.translation: You should drink plenty and rest.
sentences.note: Sollten gives advice more gently than sollen.

sentences.text: Brauche ich für dieses Medikament ein Rezept?
sentences.translation: Do I need a prescription for this medicine?
sentences.note: Für takes the accusative case: dieses Medikament.

grammar.title: Ongoing situations with seit
grammar.explanation: Use seit with the present tense for something that began in the past and is still true now. Seit gestern names the starting point; seit zwei Tagen names the duration.
grammar.pattern: present tense + seit + starting point or duration

examples.source: Ich bin seit Montag krank.
examples.translation: I have been ill since Monday.

examples.source: Ich habe seit zwei Tagen Husten.
examples.translation: I have had a cough for two days.

grammar.commonMistake: Do not copy the English past form; an ongoing condition normally stays in the German present tense.

questions.explanation: Das Rezept is the document needed for certain medicines.

Seit introduces a duration that continues into the present.

coreVocabulary.lemma: Wie hast du auf die Nachricht reagiert?
coreVocabulary.translation: How did you react to the news?

coreVocabulary.lemma: Wir verstehen uns normalerweise sehr gut.
coreVocabulary.translation: We normally get along very well.
This time I have a different opinion.

coreVocabulary.lemma: Ich stimme dir in diesem Punkt zu.
coreVocabulary.translation: I agree with you on this point.

coreVocabulary.lemma: Obwohl wir diskutieren, bleiben wir freundlich.
coreVocabulary.translation: Although we are discussing, we remain friendly.
